ingredients.text: 4 tablespoons whole milk (or: 1 1/3 tbsp of DRY milk + 8 tablespoons of water)
1/2 package of instant rapid rise yeast
butter (1tbsp) and buttermilk (from dry, totaling about 1/3 cup) for brushing top of biscuits before placing into oven

instructions.text: •Empty the ingredients for Tangzhong Mix into a frying pan.
•Cook, stirring constantly until looks like sticky mashed potatoes (about 1min@ medium heat).
•Let cooked tangzhong sit to room temperature
•Meanwhile in a separate bowl, combining the dry ingredients of the Biscuit Mix.
•Add cooked and cool tangzhong to dry biscuit mix, along with five tablespoons of cut unsalted butter, and 1 cup of cool water.
•Sit to rise at leas 1-2 hours after lightly folding
•Mix gently, basic incorporation. Do not over knead or overmix.
•Put mix on floured surface, gently fold into layers for about 5 minutes
•Cut into 3” biscuits about 1/2” to 1” desired thickness (1” preferable).
•After biscuits are cut, let rise at room temperature for one hour, then chill for at least 15 minutes.
•For best biscuits -- prior to folding, cutting and rise; let dough rise in refrigerator for at least 4 days.
•Cover dough with 2-3Tbsp melted butter before refrigeration and keep dough airtight.
•Brush tops with buttermilk top-wash before putting in oven.
•Bake @ 400F for around 5-10 minutes until tops are golden crispy
